question: Why is navigator.mediaDevices absent on iOS, and is the custom URL scheme the cause?
method: One app, two WKWebViews, same process and same Info.plist: one at http://localhost:8128, one at chatterang://localhost served by a WKURLSchemeHandler (which is what capacitor:// is). Only the scheme varies. Then the same pair re-run with NSCameraUsageDescription added, and again with it removed.

runs.note: Flips back, so the effect is the plist key and not install order or caching.

findings.schemeIsNotTheCause: An http origin in the same WKWebView is equally blind without the usage string. #128's stated best explanation is falsified.
findings.usageStringIsTheGate: NSCameraUsageDescription toggles navigator.mediaDevices on and off at BOTH origins, on the same binary.
findings.decoderStillMissing: BarcodeDetector is absent in WKWebView at both origins AND in mobile Safari. iOS needs a bundled decoder under every option.

caveats: The simulator has no camera: this measures API SURFACE, not capture or decode. enumerateDevices returned audioinput only.
iOS 26.5 only. Older iOS runtimes not measured (see #223).

Measured in a bare WKWebView, not Capacitor's. The custom-scheme arm matches capacitor:// in the respect that matters, but confirming in a real chatterang build with the plist string added is the remaining step.
